items.title: Geometric irreducibility is Zariski local modulo connectedness: four equivalent formulations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives four equivalent conditions for a scheme X over a field k: geometric irreducibility of X, geometric irreducibility of the coordinate ring of every nonempty affine open, irreducibility of X plus geometric irreducibility of the coordinate rings of the members of one affine open covering, and the existence of a nonempty open covering by geometrically irreducible pieces which pairwise intersect; it also records that every nonempty open subscheme of a geometrically irreducible scheme is geometrically irreducible (statement lines 1404-1426). The proof reduces the affine case to the algebra definition, then uses the topological facts that irreducibility passes to nonempty opens, that two nonempty opens of an irreducible space meet, and that a scheme whose affine opens are all irreducible is irreducible; the easy implications follow, and the last condition implies irreducibility after every base change because a cover by pairwise intersecting irreducible opens stays of that form (proof lines 1428-1442). The claim is H2: a short cycle of implications whose content is the observation that the last condition is stable under base change, making it a Zariski-local criterion.
